correctness.rationale: The tangent series converges on |z|<π/2 and its coefficients are all positive by the recurrence from T′=1+T². Removing the linear term bounds |N(z)| by A(|z|). Equality at positive radius requires the cubic and quintic terms to have the same argument, hence z²>0. A(t)/t increases strictly from 0 to infinity, so the unique R solves A(R)=R and A contracts radii below R. Monotonicity and closure of [0,R] under A give the iterated upper bound without hitting a pole; oddness and N(r)=−A(r) show both real extremizers attain it. For n≥1 and r>0 these are the only maximizers; at n=0 all boundary points attain the same maximum. Since A(t)/t³ increases, iteration of the cubic bound on [0,r] gives the claimed exponent (3ⁿ−1)/2 for r<R. The open disk is connected and attracts to zero. Each nonreal point of its critical circle maps into the disk and belongs to the immediate component by its radial segment to zero. The two real points alternate and obstruct any larger centered disk; |N′(±R)|=A′(R)>A(R)/R=1, giving repulsion under the return map. π-periodicity of tangent translates the statement. An independent bounded calculation gave R≈1.165561185207211 and passed 135 sampled root, orbit and modulus checks; the supplied check.py was inspected, not rerun. Neither numerical check establishes the universal claims.
